details:
BEYOND THE SILENCE is an interactive educational space mission design game inspired by the Fermi Paradox: if the universe is so vast and ancient, why have we not yet detected convincing evidence of extraterrestrial life or technological civilisations?

The game places users in the role of a mission director, challenging them to design and manage a simulated space observatory capable of investigating distant worlds. Players choose a scientific objective – biological signatures, technological signatures or both – before selecting scientific instruments and an orbital destination. They must balance engineering constraints, including spacecraft mass, power consumption, budget, data storage, communications and mission duration. Once the mission is launched, the game generates simulated scientific observations and random mission events, before producing a report evaluating the mission’s scientific value, engineering reliability and resource efficiency.

The scientific concept builds on my EPQ research into the Fermi Paradox and the possibility of detecting both biological and technological signatures. Biological investigations include potential atmospheric indicators such as methane and oxygen, while technological investigations explore unusual infrared emissions and possible artificial radio signals. The proposed observatory draws inspiration from real space telescopes, particularly the James Webb Space Telescope, and uses Sun–Earth L2 as one of its possible orbital destinations.

The project’s main benefit is making complex astrophysics and spacecraft engineering more accessible through interactive learning. Instead of simply reading about space missions, users experience the compromises involved in designing one. It encourages critical thinking by showing that potential signs of life are not automatically proof of extraterrestrial intelligence or even biological activity; natural explanations and false positives must be considered.

The intended impact is to inspire interest in STEM, particularly aerospace engineering, astronomy and astrobiology, while helping users understand the scientific and engineering challenges involved in searching for extraterrestrial life. It also demonstrates that even when a mission finds no convincing evidence, its observations can still contribute to scientific understanding.

The game was developed using Python, with Tkinter for its graphical user interface, and Thonny as the development environment. It was designed to run on a computer without requiring specialist spacecraft hardware. Replit was then used to turn the Python Tkinter game into an accessible and playable browser link.

Its creativity comes from combining the mystery of the Fermi Paradox with an interactive mission-management experience. It connects scientific exploration with practical engineering decisions, allowing players to see how different instruments and mission configurations influence what a spacecraft can investigate.

During development, the team considered scientific relevance, instrument capabilities, spacecraft mass, power requirements, budget, data generation, communication capacity, orbital environment and mission reliability. Accessibility and educational value were also important considerations. The game uses simplified engineering values and fictional observations for educational purposes rather than claiming to be a fully accurate spacecraft simulator.

BEYOND THE SILENCE transforms the question of whether we are alone in the universe into an opportunity to explore how humanity might investigate that possibility.

AI Disclosure: We used ChatGPT and Claude to assist with code generation, debugging, interface development, and brainstorming, as well as to help draft, structure, and edit the text for our Project Summary and Project Details. All core scientific concepts, EPQ research foundations, and final design decisions were created, reviewed, and adapted by our team.
